How the quantities were determined

I used a weighted average of recent sales, with 70% weight on October–November 2025 and 30% on September–November 2025. The calculation then covers each supplier's lead time plus the review period, adds safety stock, and subtracts usable inventory and all 126 confirmed incoming-delivery lines. Finally, it rounds orders to supplier minimums and multiples.

For example, the recommended orders include 20 Notebook Packs for London, 20 Desk Fans for Manchester, and 15 Vision 27 Monitors for New York.

These are recommended quantities for orders placed December 1, rather than quantities guaranteed to arrive during December 1–7. Supplier lead times determine the expected arrival of new orders, while deliveries already scheduled for that week are accounted for separately.

The Excel workbook is the main deliverable: it gives you the exact quantities to purchase for every store and product, with the inputs needed to audit each recommendation.
